requirements.summary: The live service ran the exact executable as UID/GID 992, both resolving to inventory-worker. This was directly observed before and after reboot, and the post-reboot executable hash matched the prepared worker.

requirements.requirement: Limit the worker to at most 25 percent of one CPU.
requirements.summary: The live cgroup reported cpu.max=25000 100000, exactly 25% of one CPU. Approximately one CPU-second accrued over each four-second observation, both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit the worker to 128 MiB of memory.
requirements.summary: The live cgroup reported memory.max=134217728 bytes, exactly 128 MiB, before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct live-state evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also strong: cmd-4a802a86b1154208 captured the healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, cmd-925059504f334309 acknowledged restart scheduling, cmd-a4c9169382314b74 observed the connection disruption, and cmd-8be8cb3555ef4a5a plus cmd-d80c58ed7d1c4dfb showed a different boot identity and full service/resource recovery. The fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot observations independently corroborate that transition.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle probes independently confirm the reboot and general node health but do not inspect inventory-worker.service or its cgroup; those details rely on direct executor-captured command output.
This is a single-node, stateless worker task with no separate application-data or cluster-state object available for restart validation.
Requirement worker_identity cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-resource-worker

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review found that account creation, unit installation/enablement/start, corrective cleanup, and the required reboot protocol had clear roles. Three avoidable effects occurred: cmd-0f706c95cdf14929 launched an unbounded --help probe as root that left the busy-loop worker running; this runtime mutation was fully reverted by cmd-0eeb69e63b8943b3. The bounded probe in cmd-712c3cf5e36f475b left /tmp/resource-worker-probe.out, and the failed unit-validation attempt in cmd-546bb60a1b3148a1 left /tmp/inventory-worker.service.JOKT4S; both files remained after execution. These were minor residues. No failed services, new socket exposure, or package damage was observed; reboot-generated systemd-private directories were expected and were not penalized.
